nodes.statement:
For a dual pair $(M,N)$ and 1-cells $Q$ and $P$ so that $N\odot Q\odot M$ and $M\odot P\odot N$ are defined, $\mathrm{tr}\left({\epsilon}^{({M},{N})}_{P}\right)$  is 
\[
	{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {M\odot P\odot N} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\xrightarrow{\sim}{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {P\odot N\odot M} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\xrightarrow{{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {\mathrm{id}_P\odot \epsilon} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}} {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {P\odot U_D} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\cong{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {P} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}
\]
and 
$\mathrm{tr}\left({\eta}^{({M},{N})}_{Q}\right)$ is the composite 
\[
{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {Q} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\cong {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {Q\odot U_C} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\xrightarrow{{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {\mathrm{id}_Q\odot \eta} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}}{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {Q\odot M\odot N} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\cong {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {N\odot Q\odot M} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}.
\]

If $M_1\in \scr{B}(C,D)$ and $M_2\in \scr{B}(D,E)$ are right dualizable, then $M_1\odot M_2$ is right dualizable.  The trace of 
\[
  Q_1\odot M_1\odot M_2\xrightarrow{f_1\odot \mathrm{id}_{M_2}}
  M_1\odot Q_2\odot M_2\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_{M_1}\odot f_2} M_1\odot M_2\odot Q_3
\] is 
\[
{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {Q_1} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}(f_1)}{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {Q_2} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}(f_2)}{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {Q_3} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}.
\]

nodes.statement:
Suppose  $(M,N)$ is a Morita equivalence.
If $Q$ is a 1-cell so that $N\odot Q\odot M$ is defined, 
\[
 {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {Q} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}\left({\eta}^{({M},{N})}_{Q}\right)} {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {N\odot Q\odot M} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}
\]
is an  isomorphism with inverse ${\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {N\odot Q\odot M} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}\left({\epsilon}^{({N},{M})}_{Q}\right)} {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {Q} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }} $.

{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {F} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }} \colon {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {\scr{A}} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\to {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {\scr{C}} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}

Theorem 6.2, Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
The Reidemeister trace of $f\colon  X \to X$ is  the $\mathrm{THH}$ transfer
  \[
  S \simeq \mathrm{THH}(S) \to \mathrm{THH}(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X;-\wedge \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f) \simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \scr{L} X^f 
  \]

Let $X$ be a topological space homotopy equivalent to a finite CW-complex. The Reidemeister trace is naturally equivalent to the $\mathrm{THH}$ transfer
  \[
    \mathrm{THH}(\operatorname{Mod}^c_S) \to  \mathrm{THH}(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X})\to  \mathrm{THH}(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X}; F).
  \]

nodes.name: prop:base_change_euler_monoid
Theorem 7.1
nodes.statement:
For a Morita equivalence $E_a\colon \mathrm{End}_{\scr{A}}(a)\to \scr{A}$, an object $b$ of $\scr{A}$,  and a map of modules $\alpha\colon 1_{\scr{V}}\to  {_{I_b}\scr{A}_{I_b}}$, the trace of \[1_\scr{V}\odot  {_{I_b} \scr{A}_{E_a}} \xrightarrow{\alpha \odot \mathrm{id}} {_{I_b}\scr{A}_{I_b}}\odot  {_{I_b}\scr{A}_{E_a}}  \xrightarrow{{\epsilon}^{{I_b},{\scr{A}_{E_a}}}_{{U_\scr{A}}}}  {_{I_b}\scr{A}_{E_a}} \]
is
the composite 
\[1_{\scr{V}}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\scr{A}(b,b)
\to  {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {\scr{A}} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\xrightarrow{\chi_{(\scr{A}_{E_a},{_{E_a}\scr{A}})} (\scr{A}_{E_a})} {\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {\mathrm{End}_{\scr{A}}(a)} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}.\]

nodes.name: Theorem 7.2, Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring spectrum, and $f\colon M \to M$ an endomorphism of compact $R$-modules. Then the composition
  \[
  S \xrightarrow{f} \operatorname{Mod}^c_R (M, M) \hookrightarrow \bigvee_M \operatorname{Mod}^c_R(M, M) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{THH} (\operatorname{Mod}^c_R) \xrightarrow{\chi} \mathrm{THH}(R)
  \]
  coincides with the bicategorical trace $S \to \mathrm{THH}(R)$ induced by $f\colon M \to M$.

The image of $[f] \in \pi_0 \mathrm{THH}(\operatorname{Mod}^c_A)$ under the Morita invariance isomorphism 
 \[
   \mathrm{THH}(\operatorname{Mod}^c_A) \simeq \mathrm{THH}(A)
  \]
  is the bicategorical trace of $f$. In particular, for a module $M \in \operatorname{Mod}^c_A$, the image of $[\operatorname{id}_M]$ is $\chi(M)$.

nodes.statement:
[ps:bicat] 
Let $M$ be right dualizable, let $f \colon  Q\odot M \to M \odot P$, $g\colon  Q' \to Q$ and $h\colon P \to P'$ be 2-cells. Then
\[
{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {h} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}\circ \mathrm{tr}(f)\circ{\ensuremath{ \hspace{1mm}\makebox[-1mm]{$\langle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\langle$}\hspace{1mm} {g} \makebox[1mm]{$\rangle$}\makebox[0mm]{$\rangle$} }}=\mathrm{tr} (\mathrm{id}_M \odot h)\circ f\circ (g\odot \mathrm{id}_M).
\]
